name: Wei Okafor

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What is a normal workday like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and lead a carpentry crew setting roof trusses on new housing sites. My vocational trade certificate led to years of lift work, and the complex trusses pay above the ordinary trade rate, though I still check every bearing myself. I like watching a roof take shape; waiting for missing brackets is the part that wastes a day.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like, and do you use AI tools?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works at a library, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. We've saved about ten months of expenses and there are plenty of other builders nearby. I use AI every day for bracket lists and lift plans, then compare them with the engineer's drawing; I also attend our builders' union safety meetings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew AI can shorten the timber order, but the roof truss still has to sit on a level bearing. A small gain is welcome if the people lifting it keep their time and pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I lead the housing-site truss crew and my pay is above the usual carpentry rate. My partner's library wage, ten months of saved expenses and plentiful nearby builders mean this mild picture leaves our mortgage comfortable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll carry on setting the roof trusses and use my daily AI ordering tool to check counts against the engineer's drawing. At the next builders' union safety meeting I'll bring a request for paid time to teach the youngest crew member how to check each bearing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about our income and pleased if the lists take less time. I still want an actual pair of eyes on the truss seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When did the order list miss something?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yesterday the list gave us twelve brackets when the drawing called for fourteen at the end bay. We corrected the roof truss bracket order before the truck came.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the paid teaching proposal include?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would name the bearing check, the apprentice's paid hours and the fitter who signs off the work. The union meeting can put that full proposal to the contractor.

say: **AI ordering** can save time, but truss bearings still need physical checks.
**Paid apprentice time** should remain in the site plan.
think: My **higher carpentry wage** and partner's library job support the mortgage.
Ten months of **saved expenses** and nearby builders make a small change comfortable.
do: **Set** housing-site roof trusses and check AI bracket counts against drawings.
**Bring** paid truss-bearing lesson to next builders' union safety meeting.
feel: **Calm** about stable wages and useful daily AI.
S0.quote: We corrected the roof truss bracket order before the truck came.
fieldNote: He catches a **missing bracket count** by comparing his daily AI list to the engineer's drawing.
His **union lesson proposal** specifies paid apprentice hours and sign-off; strong income and savings support calm.

steps.text: Set housing-site trusses and check AI bracket counts against drawings
Bring paid truss-bearing lesson to builders union safety meeting

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew AI may take over buying and checklists before robots can lift trusses safely. I'd support the new planner if workers can correct it and still stop a dangerous lift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own higher-paid fitting role looks secure while office tasks change. I worry the new schedule could hurry crane lifts, but with nearby builders and our reserve I have room to speak up without fearing next week's bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll learn the contractor's new AI lift-sequencing controls on one empty test bay and compare its timing with our measured rigging and crane plan. At the site union meeting I'll ask for a named worker's stop authority in any automated schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about a rushed lift, but my income feels secure for now. I like testing a useful tool early, with the crane stopped while we check it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do at a rushed lift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd stop the lift, check the bearing and call the crane operator back to the marked position. A screen's green tick cannot see a loose sling above someone's head.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why try the new sequencing controls on an empty bay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the proposed lift order with the real crane reach and record any correction. The test bay is empty, so no other trade is beneath us while I learn the controls.

say: **AI buying and planning** will change before hands-on truss robots spread.
Workers need **edit and stop authority** over lift schedules.
think: My **higher-paid lead role** still looks secure.
Rushed crane work would create **safety pressure**, even with strong savings and nearby jobs.
do: **Learn** AI lift-sequencing controls on an empty test bay.
**Compare** planned lifts with rigging and crane reach before use.
**Ask** site union for named worker stop authority.
feel: **Uneasy** about lift safety, with my wage secure.
S1.quote: A screen's green tick cannot see a loose sling above someone's head.
fieldNote: He learns **new AI controls** early on a test bay and validates them against rigging and crane reach.
His **union request** concerns stop authority; he does not claim his own income will shrink in this slower change.

steps.text: Learn AI lift sequencing on empty test bay
Compare planned lifts with measured rigging and crane reach
Ask site union for named worker stop authority

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew thinking AI by 2028 could plan every truss lift, then capable robots around 2031 could set the roofs. A contractor should publish paid crew numbers before calling a machine an improvement for workers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd be about 48 when robots can do the physical lift. If half our truss shifts vanish, ten months saved and many nearby builders buy time, but we would still need a mortgage wage and those builders might buy robots too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask the builders' union to negotiate a paid site-robot trial with a worker able to halt lifts. If our contractor offers a funded, recognised machine-rigging course with full wages through class days, I'll enrol and attend; if my shifts are cut first, I'll apply to posted local construction posts with reliable hours and pay that covers our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about possible lost shifts, with money and skills to make a move. I will not call watching a demonstration a new qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a safe robot lift trial look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd test a truss on an uneven bearing with a clear exclusion area below the lift. A perfect roof-truss robot demonstration in a yard would hide the places a real roof gives a machine trouble.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a training or job offer real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want a written course place, fees paid and full wages on training days. Any other site post would need a posted local vacancy and reliable mortgage-covering pay before I left this crew.

say: **2028 thinking AI** plans lifts before robots set trusses around 2031.
Workers need **published crew numbers** and paid safety trials.
think: At about **48**, robot lifts could cut my paid shifts.
Ten months of **savings** and nearby builders help, but the mortgage still needs wages.
do: **Ask** builders' union for paid robot trial and stop authority.
**Enrol** in funded recognised rigging course if full wages continue during class.
**Apply** after cuts to posted local construction job with reliable mortgage-covering pay.
feel: **Anxious** about possible shift cuts, with a strong buffer and options.
S2.quote: A perfect roof-truss robot demonstration in a yard would hide the places a real roof gives a machine trouble.
fieldNote: He requires **paid trial safety**, an exclusion area and worker stop authority before accepting robot lift claims.
Course and job moves retain **funding and wages** during class, then a posted local vacancy with mortgage-covering pay conditions.

steps.text: Ask builders union for paid robot trial and worker stop authority
Enrol in funded recognised rigging course if full class wages continue
Apply after shifts cut to posted local construction job with reliable mortgage-covering pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI by 2031 will change lift plans, and robots around 2034 could do the hands-on truss setting. Five years is time to train real workers and work out where the crane must still stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd be about 51 when robots set roofs as well as people. My high-paid role could shrink, but the longer warning lets us save new money and qualify for equipment inspection without leaving the current crew.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This winter I'll take the free evening introduction to lifting-equipment inspection at the trade centre. If the contractor funds the recognised inspection certificate with paid assessment leave and an actual place, I'll enrol next year; my partner and I will add one hundred from each full paid month to mortgage principal while our wages hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a later cut to the lead shifts, but able to use five years. I can test the first course without giving up a day of paid roofing work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would inspection cover on a robot lift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd inspect the sling, locking pins and bearing before the robot lifts. A roof-truss robot's log should record sling, pin and bearing checks so a worker can stop a lift if a pin is missing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would extra mortgage payments come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra hundred comes from future wages after our bills, not from moving ten months of savings around. We would stop the extra payment if a full paid month did not arrive.

say: **2031 thinking AI** changes lift plans before robots set trusses around 2034.
Workers need **equipment inspection skills** and stop authority.
think: At about **51**, my lead shifts could shrink with robot lifts.
Five years supports **new study** and loan payments while wages remain.
do: **Attend** free evening lifting-inspection introduction this winter.
**Enrol** in recognised certificate if funded place and paid assessment leave secured.
**Pay extra** mortgage principal from each full paid month while wages hold.
feel: **Anxious** about later shifts, with time for study and saving.
S3.quote: A roof-truss robot's log should record sling, pin and bearing checks so a worker can stop a lift if a pin is missing.
fieldNote: He starts **actual free study** and makes the recognised course conditional on funded fees, a real place and paid assessment leave.
His **new loan payments** come from future full paid months, preserving the existing ten-month reserve.

steps.text: Enrol in recognised inspection certificate if funded place and paid leave secured
Pay extra mortgage principal from future full paid months while wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI by 2036 may plan roofs, then capable robots around 2039 may set trusses. Ten years is long enough to build a proper worker training route and teach the next crew safe lifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd be about 56 when robots do the physical setting, and our children will be older. I cannot promise the mortgage will be finished, but ten months of saved expenses, higher pay and plentiful local builders make a careful transition possible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep my lifting safety certificate current and bring a paid robot-inspection apprenticeship plan to the next union training committee. If a recognised inspection course gets a funded place and paid time, I'll enrol; after qualifying I would apply only to posted local inspection jobs with reliable hours and mortgage-covering wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about our own near-term income, interested in shaping the longer transition. Ten years lets me prepare without pretending the builders will never change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What belongs in an apprentice lift session?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd put a working lift, a sling check and a stop signal into every apprentice's paid practice. A roof-truss apprentice should have a named fitter beside them, not just a machine screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would the committee turn this into a proposal?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The union committee can put the paid hours, instructor and certificate requirement into one proposal to the builder. I would bring our current lift checklist so the plan starts from a real site task.

say: **2036 thinking AI** plans roofs before robots set trusses around 2039.
A decade permits **paid apprenticeships** and inspection qualifications.
think: At about **56**, I may still need site wages if the mortgage remains.
Our **ten-month reserve** and local jobs make the near term secure.
do: **Bring** paid robot-inspection apprenticeship plan to union training committee.
**Enrol** in recognised inspection course if funded place and paid time secured.
**Apply** after qualifying to posted local inspection job with reliable mortgage-covering pay.
feel: **Calm** about near-term income, engaged with a long transition.
S4.quote: A roof-truss apprentice should have a named fitter beside them, not just a machine screen.
fieldNote: His **union committee plan** specifies paid practice, an instructor and a recognised certificate, grounded in actual lifting checks.
Training and any later job move require **funded paid time** and qualification, followed by a posted local role with adequate wages.

steps.text: Bring paid robot-inspection apprenticeship plan to union training committee
Enrol in recognised inspection course if funded place and paid time secured
Apply after qualifying to posted local inspection job with reliable mortgage-covering pay

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because capable truss robots around 2031 could cut well-paid lift shifts while we still need a mortgage wage. Published crew numbers, a paid safe trial and a funded course with full wages would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who signs the lift sheet after a robot sets a truss on a crooked bearing. A robot can lower a roof truss perfectly onto the wrong timber. I want a trained worker there before the crane line comes off.

headlineQuote: A robot can lower a roof truss perfectly onto the wrong timber.
portrait: **Wei**, 43, leads housing-site truss work with a vocational certificate, high practical skill and above-average trade pay.
His library-worker partner, two children and **mortgage** share ten months of savings and plentiful nearby construction alternatives.
He uses **AI daily** for lists and plans, tests new controls early and brings safety terms to his builders' union.
Fast robot lifts make him **anxious** about paid shifts; a decade gives him time to seek funded inspection training.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could bring capable truss robots around 2031 while his well-paid shifts support a mortgage.
whatWouldHelp: **Published crew numbers**, a paid safe trial and funded training with full wages would help him prepare.
